messages:
nora-support: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s and high tail latency on /v1/generate after the staged rollout around 08:07 UTC. Lots of request IDs: req=ZQ9f... please triage.
kevin-choi: I see the spike in SLO dashboard, p50 fine, p95+p99 up. Alerting channel lit. Any recent deploys? :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy started: staged-release/2026-03-17T08:05 by @maya-patel on pool=seed-2, config=auth-rotation-v2
maya-patel: that deploy included the auth header sanitizer/rotation. rolling to 10% traffic.
samir-ops: customers say timeouts, not straight 500s. Are we dropping or truncating Authorization header upstream?
elena-reliability: traces show Gateway->Authz service timeouts. A ton of 504s with error "upstream read timeout". Also seeing 502 from api-router when request body size small.
nora-support: customer A (acct: acme-corp) opened a P1: "sudden errors, punting requests to the app are failing and billing is impacted." They gave sample curl with X-Request-Id header.
kevin-choi: can someone paste a repro curl from prod logs? need exact headers.
maya-patel: from logs:

curl -v "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'

response: 502 Bad Gateway, upstream: "authz: malformed header"
samir-ops: looking at the auth-rotation code — it switches to a short-key fingerprint header when token length > 1024. There was an off-by-one on slice length. If header hits exactly 1024 it's truncated to 0-length token.
elena-reliability: that explains spikes for certain JWT sizes. But why timeouts? truncated header causes auth service to perform heavy fallback logic hitting DB and timing out under load.
kevin-choi: quick check: grep router logs for "malformed header" and sample req ids: ZQ9f34, JH3k12, PL0b99. I see these concentrated on seed-2 (staged pool).
nora-support: customers want ETA. They report timeouts starting 08:07 UTC — correlates with deployment.
maya-patel: mitigation options: 1) rollback staged-release to previous config, 2) disable header-sanitizer flag via config flip, 3) route traffic off seed-2 to pool stable-1.
samir-ops: I can flip routing with short command. Suggest removing seed-2 from the live routing table for now. Will that avoid rollback churn?
elena-reliability: routing change cheap. But if auth-service DB still overloaded it might propagate. Prefer flip sanitizer flag first so tokens pass through unchanged.
kevin-choi: how to flip flag quickly?
maya-patel: config key: feature.authz.sanitizer.enabled = true -> false. It's a dynamic config via config-store. I can flip now and monitor.
deploy-bot: config change applied: feature.authz.sanitizer.enabled=false by @maya-patel at 08:24 UTC
nora-support: :thumbsup: patch noted. Customers testing — acme-corp says errors dropped to near zero for them.
elena-reliability: p95 is dropping but p99 still elevated; some queues backlogged in auth service. I'll scale auth workers and evict heavy DB reads.
samir-ops: scaled auth-service replica count +3. cleared DB query queue.
kevin-choi: rolling window shows 504s down from 18% -> 0.8% in staged pool. Good.
maya-patel: still want staged-release rollback? we can roll forward a patch to fix off-by-one in sanitizer logic and re-enable.
elena-reliability: agree. We should keep sanitizer disabled until patch deployed and verified in an isolated canary.
samir-ops: assigning owners: maya -> patch and patch deploy. elena -> auth-service scaling/monitoring. kevin -> routing and customer comms. nora -> coordinate customer updates.
nora-support: sending update to affected customers: "We're mitigating — feature sanitizer disabled; service scaling in progress; root cause identified as header truncation during auth header rotation. ETA for full resolution 45m." I'll paste in this thread once sent.
kevin-choi: small follow-up: need log pruning for request bodies with long tokens — avoid logging full auth header. Also confirm we didn't leak tokens in debug logs during this incident.
maya-patel: confirmed we weren't logging full token (we log hash) but sanitizer bug did cause some stack traces with token length metadata only. No full-token leak.
elena-reliability: postmortem notes to include: - off-by-one slice in auth sanitizer - insufficient unit coverage for boundary token lengths - staged pool routing defaulted too much traffic (10%) for this change - rollback/runbook steps were valid and executed quickly.
kevin-choi: add customer billing check: finance, please review if customers should receive credits for failed requests during window 08:07-08:30 UTC.
samir-ops: created follow-up ticket INF-1129 to add unit tests and enforce canary traffic cap for auth-related changes.
nora-support: customer update sent: "Issue mitigated — we disabled the sanitizer and scaled the auth service. Engineers are patching the sanitizer logic and will re-run rollout behind a tighter canary. We'll follow up with timeline and credits if needed." customer replied with :raised_hands: thanks.
maya-patel: patch merged to main (fix/sanitizer-boundary) and queued for canary deploy to small internal pool.
kevin-choi: once canary passes we'll schedule a gradual rollout with gate at 1%, 2%, 5% and auto-rollback on p99 increase > 50%.
elena-reliability: logging note: add an alert for sudden rise in "malformed header" specifically; current alerting groups only on 5xx rate.
samir-ops: closing the immediate incident channel. will leave this thread for postmortem entries and any customer follow-ups.
nora-support: thanks all — closing loop with customers and will attach repro logs and timeline to the ticket.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: patch canary to pool=internal-qa at 09:07 UTC by @maya-patel
kevin-choi: thanks team. Follow-ups: postmortem, bill review, unit tests, canary traffic caps. I'll create the postmortem doc and link here.
_meta: do not include title field per agents.md; messages are in chronological order; thread contains root + replies
